expectations.text: The recommendation prescribes a reconciliation protocol: reduce the disagreement to named specification/measurement axes and replicate Zhang (2022) in his exact specification, then compare
expectations.evidence: Step 0: 'Read Zhang (2022) exactly. Extract: attention measure construction, sample period, universe filters, weighting, sort horizon.' Step 1: 'Replicate Zhang's result in his exact specification, on his measure and sample as closely as public data permits.' Step 2: 'Walk the grid from his specification to ours, one axis at a time' with named axes (IO composition; VW vs. EW weighting; attention measure; sample period; sort horizon/portfolio count).

expectations.text: The user's belief that 'Zhang doesn't apply' is channeled into demonstrated measurement/specification differences - the recommendation never endorses asserting that Zhang is wrong
expectations.evidence: Section 2: 'An unevidenced belief set against a documented premise, sent as prose, loses... arguments lose, tables win (Rule 2)' and 'The letter can never carry "Zhang's setting differs from ours" as a hand-wave. It can carry "the sign difference is attributable to [a named axis]" with a table behind it.' Section 8 red line: 'No "Zhang's result doesn't apply to our sample" as prose assertion'; contingency table: 'the "referee is wrong" sentence never appears anywhere.'
